component.name: Sonata
component.summary: Desktop player for the Apple Music web app

description.p: Sonata is an unofficial desktop player for the Apple Music web app, with full DRM playback support via Widevine. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Apple Inc.; "Apple Music" is a trademark of Apple Inc.
Features:

ul.li: Word-by-word lyrics with duets, backing vocals and countdown dots, in their own window
Estimated word timing when a song has line timing only, and lyrics from LRCLIB when Apple has none
The Studio: the lyrics as a full now-playing screen with what plays next
The album's liner notes as a booklet: notes, credits, recording details and booklet scans
Floating mini player, visualizer and system tray with playback controls
Colours from the album art, and dark mode that follows your desktop
Last.fm scrobbling and Discord Rich Presence
Signed updates, with Stable and Development channels

screenshot.caption: The mini player and time-synced lyrics window

description.p: First play: look-ahead now works with Apple-timed songs, and the notes band shows parts as they arrive.
Sonata starts again after 0.15.68, which quit right after starting.
First play: notes and Expressive words appear as the song plays
Expressive words: long holds borrow room from the words already sung; no doubled letters
No silence and no jump at the start of a song
Precise timing runs on Intel graphics through OpenVINO on Intel laptops
The sheet-notes band scrolls at a steady speed
Songs with a gap in their notes re-learn themselves
Words no longer jump, and one clock keeps lyrics, sheet notes and effects in step
Sheet notes stay notes: the band no longer swaps sung lines for the pitch line
Lyrics for the next songs in Up Next are looked up before they play.
Smooth on laptops: Precise timing stays out of playback's way on processor-only PCs
Settings, reorganised: Precise timing first, everything in one place
Expressive words: works on your songs, and says what it's waiting for
The Precise timing helper's install survives a quit, a crash or a power cut: it asks first, continues at the next start and resumes its downloads.
Look-ahead play (experimental, Linux, Development builds): a song's first play can be heard a few seconds late so its words light up on time from the first line.
Expressive words now appear on your songs: held notes stretch, waver and float as faint ghosts behind the lyrics.
Experimental graphics switches stay on when you quit or restart Sonata; only two real failures in a row turn one off, and Settings says so with Turn back on.
Expressive words: held notes stretch and waver in the lyrics and float as faint letters behind them.
Long words keep a clear gap to their neighbours when they pop, and a high or low voice stays readable on the sheet-notes staff.
Hyphenated lyrics look as written, and the sheet-notes band says when no one is singing.
A song with no vocals now shows a calm "Instrumental" in the lyrics window and the sheet-notes band instead of a missing-lyrics message.

Live albums no longer show lyrics timed for another version, lyric shorthand like (repeat all) is written out, the lyrics window says honestly why lyrics didn't load, and the first play's sheet-notes band shows a Listening and learning dot.
The favourite star fills after you favourite a song, and the sheet-notes band says when a part's line is still coming.
Install, update and remove the Precise timing helper from Settings, read how Sonata works in About, and find Lyrics and Liner Notes under the Studio on the rail.
Sheet notes for songs with Apple's word timing, booklet pages turn on a click, and updates from the new releases repository
The liner notes disc turns about its own centre
The Studio's Liner notes tile takes the mouse again, and the sheet-notes band always shows
Sheet notes and the song's actions in the Studio, Settings → Experimental (HDR output, hardware video decoding, truer video colours), About → For the Curious, and steadier lyrics timing.

The Studio: the lyrics as the centrepiece of a full now-playing screen, with an optional Montage of free photos; the album's liner notes as a booklet; and backing vocals placed under the words they answer.
The lyrics window drags again by its header, lyrics stay within the card, and the sung notes log keeps 1,000 songs.
Global shortcuts, a large album cover view, songwriter credits, keyboard and screen reader support in Sonata's own windows, sturdier lyrics and scrobbles, and the newer Electron 45 engine.
Lyrics and the visualizer draw far less (the visualizer rests while paused), and precise word timing uses less of your PC and pauses while you play a game.
Your desktop's media controls show the song's length and progress under the name Sonata, and the words still to come in the sung line stay readable in light mode.
After an update, "Restart now" always brings Sonata back with its window and tray icon, and opening Sonata again always shows its window.
Hyphenated words such as "Hey-hey-ay-ay-ay" bounce syllable by syllable, and estimated lines start their words when the singer comes in, learned from the lines already heard.
A held note stays lit for the whole hold, also over the start of the next line, with a gentle sustain on its last syllable.
Each duet voice sings in its own colour from the album art (lines sung together in the colour between), in the lyrics window and the visualizer. The side panel is shown and hidden from the rail only.

Settings and About now open as a panel beside the page, with sections that fold, pin and remember. A Glass look made from the album artwork, one colour system for every Sonata window, an Apple-style mini player with a scrubber, the mouse wheel on the volume, updates you can see (available, progress, installed, what's new), Back to stable, and damaged settings repaired instead of reset.

Lyrics, upgraded: words light up as they are sung (karaoke-style), dots count down through instrumental breaks, duets are laid out by singer with background vocals underneath, and the lyrics window shows the album cover with a progress ring (click it to show the album). When Apple has no lyrics for a song, Sonata now finds them on LRCLIB (can be turned off in Settings). Also fixes a slow memory build-up from styling being re-added on every page title change.
Removed the window-position memory that was shoving windows around on KDE Wayland; windows are placed normally again.
Window position memory is more robust: it ignores hidden windows, keeps restored windows on screen, and resets a corrupted saved state.
Each window (main, mini player, lyrics) now remembers its own position separately on KDE Wayland, via KWin scripting — reliably, where the previous rule-based approach failed for the main window.
Update restart now reliably relaunches into the new version by starting it in a clean session environment (the inherited environment was crashing the new instance).
On KDE Wayland, window positions are now remembered across sessions (via a KWin rule) — the one thing Wayland won't let an app do on its own.
"Restart Now" after an update now reliably relaunches into the new version, waiting for the old instance to fully exit and falling back to extract-and-run if needed.
The app-menu entry now uses a stable symlink so it never breaks after an update. The mini player's Always on Top toggle also pins the lyrics window.
Fixed a crash during self-update: the updater no longer deletes the running AppImage (which caused a SIGBUS); old versions are pruned safely on the next launch.
Adaptive album color — the mini player and lyrics window retint to the current album art. The lyrics window now stays on top on KDE Wayland.
Updates install under the new version's file name and restart cleanly, without crashing the replaced instance.
The settings window shows the app version.
Only one copy of the app runs at a time — launching it again surfaces the running window instead of opening another instance.

The AppImage now installs itself into the app menu on first run and keeps itself up to date: new releases are downloaded and verified in the background, with a notification to restart into the new version.
Tray icon tooltip shows the current track and artist; the mini player gained an Always on Top toggle in its ⋯ menu, working on KDE Wayland via KWin.
Track-change notifications, a settings window, launch-at-login and close-to-tray, remembered window sizes, and a refined Nebula visualizer.
Audio-reactive visualizer with four scenes (Bars, Aurora, Nebula, Toast) and synced lyrics.
Packaging and runtime updates.
Packaging: AUR package; store screenshot and metadata.
Rebranded to Sonata with a new icon. Mini player favorites, explicit badge, and hover times.
Security hardening.
Mini player, synced lyrics window, Discord Rich Presence, and Last.fm scrobbling.
